claim: UCH37 (also known as UCHL5) is a highly conserved deubiquitinating enzyme (DUB) that associates with the 26S proteasome.
source: UCH37, also known as UCHL5, is a highly conserved deubiquitinating enzyme (DUB) that associates with the 26S proteasome.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about UCH37.

claim: UCH37 activity is stimulated by branched ubiquitin chain architectures.
source: Recently, it was reported that UCH37 activity is stimulated by branched ubiquitin (Ub) chain architectures.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Deol et al., 2020).

claim: UCH37 is activated by contacts with the hydrophobic patches of both distal Ubs that emanate from a branched Ub.
source: To understand how UCH37 achieves its unique debranching specificity, we performed biochemical and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) structural analyses and found that UCH37 is activated by contacts with the hydrophobic patches of both distal Ubs that emanate from a branched Ub.
evidence: This claim is supported by biochemical and NMR structural analyses performed in this study.

claim: RPN13 enhances branched-chain specificity by restricting linear Ub chains from having access to the UCH37 active site.
source: In addition, RPN13, which recruits UCH37 to the proteasome, further enhances branched-chain specificity by restricting linear Ub chains from having access to the UCH37 active site.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing differential activity with linear versus branched chains in the presence of RPN13.

claim: Substrate clearance by the proteasome is promoted by both binding and deubiquitination of branched polyubiquitin by UCH37 under conditions of proteolytic stress in cultured human cells.
source: In cultured human cells under conditions of proteolytic stress, we show that substrate clearance by the proteasome is promoted by both binding and deubiquitination of branched polyubiquitin by UCH37.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-based experiments showing effects on substrate clearance.

claim: Proteasomes containing UCH37(C88A) aberrantly retain polyubiquitinated species as well as the RAD23B substrate shuttle factor.
source: Proteasomes containing UCH37(C88A), which is catalytically inactive, aberrantly retain polyubiquitinated species as well as the RAD23B substrate shuttle factor, suggesting a defect in recycling of the proteasome for the next round of substrate processing.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry data showing accumulation of polyUb and RAD23B on C88A proteasomes.

claim: The ubiquitin–proteasome system is responsible for regulated protein degradation that maintains protein homeostasis and plays a major role in the defense against proteolytic stresses.
source: In eukaryotes, the ubiquitin (Ub)–proteasome system is responsible for regulated protein degradation that maintains protein homeostasis and plays a major role in the defense against proteolytic stresses.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the ubiquitin-proteasome system.

claim: Ub in the form of a variety of polyUb chains serves as a signal that targets unwanted proteins to the 26S proteasome where the proteins are unfolded and translocated into the interior chamber of the 20S proteasome where they are degraded.
source: Ub in the form of a variety of polyUb chains serves as a signal that targets unwanted proteins to the 26S proteasome where the proteins are unfolded and translocated into the interior chamber of the 20S proteasome where they are degraded.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about proteasome function.

claim: The timing of Ub removal is critical as premature deubiquitination can lead to unintended release of the substrate, whereas failure to remove Ub can inhibit substrate translocation.
source: The timing of Ub removal is critical as premature deubiquitination can lead to unintended release of the substrate, whereas failure to remove Ub can inhibit substrate translocation.
evidence: This is based on established understanding of proteasome function and DUB activity.

claim: PolyUb chains released from the substrates need to be further disassembled in order to minimize competition with new substrates awaiting processing by the proteasome.
source: Additionally, polyUb chains released from the substrates need to be further disassembled in order to minimize competition with new substrates awaiting processing by the proteasome.
evidence: This is based on logical inference about proteasome function and substrate competition.

claim: Three DUBs are associated with the proteasome: RPN11, USP14, and UCH37.
source: Coordination of these actions relies on three DUBs associated with the proteasome: RPN11, USP14, and UCH37.
evidence: This is established knowledge about proteasome-associated DUBs.

claim: Each of the proteasome-associated DUBs (RPN11, USP14, and UCH37) has a nonredundant role in proteasome function.
source: Each of these DUBs has a nonredundant role in proteasome function.
evidence: This is based on established understanding of proteasome DUB functions.

claim: A role of UCH37 was discovered only recently (Deol et al., 2020).
source: In recent years, significant progress has been made in our understanding of how RPN11 and USP14 are regulated to coordinate with substrate processing on the 26S proteasome, a role of UCH37 was discovered only recently (Deol et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent work.

claim: RPN11 (also called POH1) is a stoichiometric subunit of the 19S regulatory particle (RP) of the proteasome.
source: RPN11 (also called POH1) is a stoichiometric subunit of the 19S regulatory particle (RP) of the proteasome; it is the only essential DUB in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
evidence: This is established knowledge about RPN11.

claim: RPN11 is the only essential DUB in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source: RPN11 (also called POH1) is a stoichiometric subunit of the 19S regulatory particle (RP) of the proteasome; it is the only essential DUB in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
evidence: This is established knowledge about RPN11 in yeast.

claim: RPN11 activity is coupled to substrate degradation by removing polyUb chains en bloc as the substrate is translocated through a narrow gate into the proteolytic chamber of the 20S proteasome.
source: RPN11 activity is coupled to substrate degradation by removing polyUb chains en bloc as the substrate is translocated through a narrow gate into the proteolytic chamber of the 20S proteasome (Yao and Cohen, 2002; Verma et al., 2002; Worden et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: USP14 (UBP6 in yeast) is a dissociable subunit of the 19S RP.
source: USP14 (UBP6 in yeast) is a dissociable subunit of the 19S RP (Leggett et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: USP14 is activated upon forming a complex with the RP and removes Ub from substrates that are ubiquitinated at multiple sites.
source: It is activated upon forming a complex with the RP and removes Ub from substrates that are ubiquitinated at multiple sites (Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: In vivo and in vitro evidence suggest that USP14/UBP6 inhibits proteasome degradation via both catalytic and noncatalytic mechanisms.
source: In vivo and in vitro evidence suggest that USP14/UBP6 inhibits proteasome degradation via both catalytic and noncatalytic mechanisms (Lee et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2010; Hanna et al., 2006; Bashore et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: USP14 can act before substrate is translocated into the 20S core particle and committed to degradation, in contrast to RPN11.
source: In contrast to RPN11, USP14 can act before substrate is translocated into the 20S core particle and committed to degradation.
evidence: This is based on established understanding of USP14 function compared to RPN11.

claim: Inhibition of proteasome-associated DUBs have broad effects on cellular proteostasis.
source: Inhibition of proteasome-associated DUBs have broad effects on cellular proteostasis (Li et al., 2017; D'Arcy et al., 2011), highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting proteasomal DUBs.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: UCH37 is a highly conserved DUB found from fission yeast to humans, but absent in the budding yeast S. cerevisiae.
source: UCH37 (also known as UCHL5) is a highly conserved DUB found from fission yeast to humans, but absent in the budding yeast S. cerevisiae.
evidence: This is established knowledge about UCH37 conservation.

claim: UCH37 has a catalytic domain characteristic of the UCH family of DUBs and a unique C-terminal domain (CTD) that mediates interactions with two binding partners, RPN13 and NFRKB.
source: It has a catalytic domain characteristic of the UCH family of DUBs and a unique C-terminal domain (CTD) that mediates interactions with two binding partners, RPN13 (Hamazaki et al., 2006; Yao et al., 2006; Qiu et al., 2006) and NFRKB.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: RPN13 (also known as ADRM1) recruits UCH37 to the 19S RP of the proteasome whereas NFRKB recruits it to the INO80 chromatin remodeler.
source: We previously reported that RPN13 (also known as ADRM1) recruits UCH37 to the 19S RP of the proteasome whereas NFRKB recruits it to the INO80 chromatin remodeler (Yao et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: UCH37 is activated upon binding RPN13, but is held inactive in the complex with INO80.
source: Remarkably, whereas UCH37 is activated upon binding RPN13, it is held inactive in the complex with INO80.
evidence: This is based on prior work by the authors.

claim: Crystal structures of UCH37 in both the activated and repressed states have been solved.
source: We and others have solved the crystal structures of UCH37 in both the activated and repressed states (Vander Linden et al., 2015; Sahtoe et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior structural work.

claim: RPN13 stabilizes UCH37 in a conformation that promotes Ub binding, whereas NFRKB represses UCH37 by occluding the Ub-binding site.
source: These structures revealed that, whereas RPN13 stabilizes UCH37 in a conformation that promotes Ub binding, NFRKB represses UCH37 by occluding the Ub-binding site.
evidence: This claim is based on structural data from prior work.

claim: Deletion of UCH37 in mice is embryonic lethal, although the underlying cause is unclear.
source: Deletion of UCH37 in mice is embryonic lethal, although the underlying cause is unclear (Al-Shami et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Cellular functions that have been associated with UCH37 include TGFβ signaling, Hedgehog signaling, DNA repair, and cell cycle regulation.
source: Cellular functions that have been associated with UCH37 include TGFβ signaling (Wicks et al., 2005), Hedgehog signaling (Zhou et al., 2018), DNA repair (Nishi et al., 2014), and cell cycle regulation (Randles et al., 2016); in these cases and others (Li et al., 2019; Jacobson et al., 2014) UCH37 was reported to either promote or inhibit degradation of a proposed substrate.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: 10–20% of polyUb chains in the cell have a branched architecture in which more than one Ub is attached to a single Ub acceptor.
source: Among the variety of polyUb polymers in the cell, 10–20% have a branched architecture (Swatek et al., 2019) in which more than one Ub is attached to a single Ub acceptor.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Branched polyUb chains have been reported to have a variety of functions.
source: Branched polyUb chains have been reported to have a variety of functions (Haakonsen and Rape, 2019); most notably, polyUb branching enhances substrate degradation by the proteasome (Yau et al., 2017; Meyer and Rape, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: PolyUb branching enhances substrate degradation by the proteasome.
source: Branched polyUb chains have been reported to have a variety of functions (Haakonsen and Rape, 2019); most notably, polyUb branching enhances substrate degradation by the proteasome (Yau et al., 2017; Meyer and Rape, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: UCH37 has a K48-linkage-specific debranching activity that promotes proteasomal degradation of substrates modified with branched polyUb.
source: Recently, Deol et al. revealed that UCH37 has a K48-linkage-specific debranching activity that promotes proteasomal degradation of substrates modified with branched polyUb (Deol et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: UCH37 binds to branched polyUb by engaging the hydrophobic patches on both distal Ubs at a branch point.
source: Our work demonstrates that UCH37 binds to branched polyUb by engaging the hydrophobic patches on both distal Ubs at a branch point.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR and biochemical data presented in the manuscript.

claim: PolyUb conjugates that accumulate upon proteolytic stresses are greatly enhanced by the loss of UCH37 activity.
source: In cells, polyUb conjugates that accumulate upon proteolytic stresses are greatly enhanced by the loss of UCH37 activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-based experiments showing increased polyUb accumulation in UCH37 KO cells.

claim: Branched Ub3 chains are strongly preferred as substrates (i.e., 10- to 100-fold faster hydrolysis) over their linear counterparts by UCH37.
source: By quantifying the release of the Ub2 and Ub1 products (Figure 1C), we drew the following conclusions: (1) The branched Ub3 chains are strongly preferred as substrates (i.e., 10- to 100-fold faster hydrolysis) over their linear counterparts (e.g., [Ub]2–6,48Ub versus Ub–6Ub–48Ub or Ub–48Ub–6Ub).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from deubiquitination assays shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Among the branched Ub3 substrates, UCH37 strongly prefers K6/K48 over K11/K48 or K48/K63 branched chains.
source: (2) Among the branched Ub3 substrates, UCH37 strongly prefers K6/K48 over K11/K48 or K48/K63 branched chains.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from deubiquitination assays shown in Figure 1C.

claim: RPN13C enhances UCH37 hydrolysis of most polyUb substrates, but strongly inhibits activity with linear K48 Ub3.
source: (3) Whereas RPN13C enhances UCH37 hydrolysis of most polyUb substrates, it strongly inhibits activity with linear K48 Ub3 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from deubiquitination assays shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ub2 and Ub1 products were always produced in a 2:1 ratio quantified by mass, which is equivalent to a 1:1 molar ratio.
source: (4) Consistently, we found that Ub2 and Ub1 products were always produced in a 2:1 ratio quantified by mass (Figure 1C), which is equivalent to a 1:1 molar ratio.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from deubiquitination assays shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Only the K48 linkage in K6/K48-branched Ub3 was cleaved by UCH37.
source: Using linkage-specific anti-Ub antibodies, we found that only the K48 linkage in K6/K48-branched Ub3 was cleaved (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), indicative of a 'debranching' activity that thus far is unique to UCH37.
evidence: This claim is supported by data using linkage-specific antibodies shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: UCH37 exclusively cleaves the K48 linkages in branched polyUb.
source: This observation is consistent with a previous report that UCH37 exclusively cleaves the K48 linkages in branched polyUb (Deol et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and is consistent with data in this manuscript.

claim: RPN13C contacts with the UCH37 ASCL play a role to enhance UCH37 substrate specificity for branched polyUb.
source: Thus, RPN13C contacts with the UCH37 ASCL play an unexpected role to enhance UCH37 substrate specificity for branched polyUb.
evidence: This claim is supported by mutagenesis data showing that ASCL mutations affect RPN13C's ability to suppress linear K48 Ub3 hydrolysis.

claim: UCH37(C88S)–RPN13C showed highest affinity for [Ub]2–6,48Ub (KD = 4.9 μM).
source: UCH37(C88S)–RPN13C showed highest affinity for [Ub]2–6,48Ub (KD = 4.9 μM) whereas its affinities for [Ub]2–11,48Ub and [Ub]2–48,63Ub were substantially weaker and similar to those for linear Ub3.
evidence: This claim is supported by microscale thermophoresis binding data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Substrate binding only partially accounts for UCH37 specificity.
source: Thus, substrate binding only partially accounts for UCH37 specificity.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that binding affinities do not fully correlate with catalytic preferences.

claim: The KM for K6/K48-branched Ub3 debranching by UCH37–RPN13C is 15.5 ± 1.5 μM.
source: Using this free Ub sensor-based assay, we determined the KM and kcat for debranching of K6/K48, K11/K48, and K48/K63 Ub3 by UCH37–RPN13C (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The kcat for K6/K48-branched Ub3 debranching by UCH37–RPN13C is 1.25 ± 0.04 min−1.
source: Using this free Ub sensor-based assay, we determined the KM and kcat for debranching of K6/K48, K11/K48, and K48/K63 Ub3 by UCH37–RPN13C (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: UCH37–RPN13C binds K6/K48-branched Ub3 in preference to K11/K48 or K48/K63 branched Ub3 based on KM values.
source: Comparison of the KM values shows that UCH37–RPN13C binds K6/K48-branched Ub3 in preference to K11/K48 or K48/K63 branched Ub3.
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data showing different KM values for different branched substrates.

claim: kcat was highest for K11/K48 Ub3 debranching by UCH37–RPN13C.
source: Unexpectedly, kcat was highest for K11/K48 Ub3; this resulted in similar catalytic efficiencies (kcat/KM) of debranching by UCH37–RPN13C for K6/K48 and K11/K48 Ub3, whereas K48/K63 Ub3 cleavage efficiency is 12–16 times lower.
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: K48/K63 Ub3 cleavage efficiency by UCH37–RPN13C is 12–16 times lower than K6/K48 and K11/K48 Ub3.
source: Unexpectedly, kcat was highest for K11/K48 Ub3; this resulted in similar catalytic efficiencies (kcat/KM) of debranching by UCH37–RPN13C for K6/K48 and K11/K48 Ub3, whereas K48/K63 Ub3 cleavage efficiency is 12–16 times lower.
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The enzyme contacts the canonical Ub hydrophobic patch residues L8, I44, and V70 of the K48-linked distal Ub.
source: For the K48-linked distal Ub, we observed that the enzyme contacts the canonical Ub hydrophobic patch residues L8, I44, and V70 (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), consistent with the reported crystal structures of the UCH37–RPN13C–Ub complex (Vander Linden et al., 2015; Sahtoe et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data shown in Figure 3A and is consistent with prior crystal structures.

claim: There were notable chemical shift perturbations (CSPs) and signal attenuations in the Ub α-helix (residues 23, 27, 29, 30, and 32–34) of the K48-linked distal Ub that did not correspond to any monoUb contacts in the UCH37–RPN13C–Ub crystal structures.
source: Additionally, there were notable chemical shift perturbations (CSPs) and signal attenuations in the Ub α-helix (residues 23, 27, 29, 30, and 32–34) that did not correspond to any monoUb contacts in the UCH37–RPN13C–Ub crystal structures.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data showing CSPs in regions not previously identified in crystal structures.

claim: Strong signal attenuations of L8 and I44 were observed for the K6-linked distal Ub.
source: For the K6-linked distal Ub, we also observed strong signal attenuations of L8 and I44 (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A K6/K48 Ub3 substrate with L8A,I44A mutations in the proximal Ub is debranched by UCH37–RPN13C at least as efficiently as the wild-type substrate.
source: Importantly, we found that a K6/K48 Ub3 substrate with L8A,I44A mutations in the proximal Ub is debranched by UCH37–RPN13C at least as efficiently as the wild-type (WT) substrate (Figure 3E), indicating that the hydrophobic patch in the proximal Ub is not required for either binding or catalysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by deubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The hydrophobic patch in the proximal Ub is not required for either binding or catalysis by UCH37–RPN13C.
source: Importantly, we found that a K6/K48 Ub3 substrate with L8A,I44A mutations in the proximal Ub is debranched by UCH37–RPN13C at least as efficiently as the wild-type (WT) substrate (Figure 3E), indicating that the hydrophobic patch in the proximal Ub is not required for either binding or catalysis.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that L8A,I44A mutations in the proximal Ub do not affect debranching efficiency.

claim: L8C on the K6-linked distal Ub significantly inhibited debranching by UCH37–RPN13C.
source: Using these variants of K6/K48 Ub3, we found that L8C on the K6-linked distal Ub significantly inhibited debranching by UCH37–RPN13C; moreover, debranching was inhibited even further by the L8Cmc derivative (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by deubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Debranching was inhibited even further by the L8Cmc derivative compared to L8C.
source: Using these variants of K6/K48 Ub3, we found that L8C on the K6-linked distal Ub significantly inhibited debranching by UCH37–RPN13C; moreover, debranching was inhibited even further by the L8Cmc derivative (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by deubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Mimic2 was debranched as efficiently as WT K6/K48 Ub3 by UCH37–RPN13C.
source: Interestingly, while with Mimic1 we observed a twofold reduced debranching rate by UCH37–RPN13C, Mimic2 was debranched as efficiently as WT K6/K48 Ub3 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by deubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The L8A,I44A-containing Mimic2 was completely refractory to UCH37–RPN13C.
source: Whereas both native Ub3 and WT Mimic2 Ub3 were debranched efficiently, the L8A,I44A-containing Mimic2 was completely refractory to UCH37–RPN13C (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by deubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: UCH37–RPN13C requires hydrophobic patch residues of both distal Ub units of the branched Ub3 substrate for its debranching activity.
source: Taken together, the results of these biochemical experiments demonstrate that UCH37–RPN13C requires hydrophobic patch residues of both distal Ub units of the branched Ub3 substrate for its debranching activity.
evidence: This is inferred from multiple biochemical experiments showing that mutations in hydrophobic patches of either distal Ub inhibit debranching.

claim: When bound to UCH37–RPN13C, both distal Ub units use their hydrophobic patches to contact the enzyme.
source: These results further support our interpretation of the NMR data as showing that, when bound to UCH37–RPN13C, both distal Ub units use their hydrophobic patches to contact the enzyme.
evidence: This is inferred from NMR data and biochemical experiments showing that hydrophobic patches of both distal Ubs are important for activity.

claim: Upon osmotic stress, UCH37 localized to proteasome foci where K48-linked polyUb was also prominent.
source: As expected, upon osmotic stress, UCH37 localized to proteasome foci where K48-linked polyUb was also prominent (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The KO cells accumulated significantly more proteasome foci in comparison with the parental cells.
source: We found that the KO cells accumulated significantly more proteasome foci in comparison with the parental cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Increased accumulation of K11/K48-branched polyUb in the proteasome foci was observed in KO cells.
source: We also observed increased accumulation of K11/K48-branched polyUb in the proteasome foci in KO cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Overexpression of WT UCH37 suppressed proteasome foci accumulation in comparison with the parental cells.
source: In comparison with the parental cells, overexpression of WT UCH37 suppressed proteasome foci accumulation, whereas overexpression of C88A or EWI mutant UCH37 had the opposite effect (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Overexpression of C88A or EWI mutant UCH37 increased proteasome foci accumulation compared to parental cells.
source: In comparison with the parental cells, overexpression of WT UCH37 suppressed proteasome foci accumulation, whereas overexpression of C88A or EWI mutant UCH37 had the opposite effect (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Although most proteasome foci appeared in the nuclei of the parental cells, there was a marked increase in cytosolic foci in KO cells.
source: Interestingly, although most proteasome foci appeared in the nuclei of the parental cells, there was also a marked increase in cytosolic foci in KO cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Similar accumulations of proteasome foci in KO cells were observed following oxidative stress.
source: Similar accumulations of proteasome foci in KO cells were observed following oxidative stress (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: UCH37 DUB activity counteracts proteasome foci formation promoted by proteolytic stress.
source: These results strongly suggest that UCH37 DUB activity counteracts proteasome foci formation promoted by proteolytic stress.
evidence: This is inferred from observations that loss of UCH37 or catalytically inactive UCH37 increases foci, while WT UCH37 decreases foci.

claim: Proteasome foci were readily detectable in KO cells even without sucrose treatment.
source: We noticed also that proteasome foci were readily detectable in KO cells even without sucrose treatment (Figure 5D), suggesting that the KO cells accumulate proteasome substrates under unperturbed conditions, which is consistent with a recent report (Osei-Amponsa et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Analysis of the whole-cell lysates from the KO cells showed accumulation of K48 and K11/K48 polyUb both with and without osmotic stress.
source: Indeed, analysis of the whole-cell lysates from the KO cells showed accumulation of K48 and K11/K48 polyUb both with and without osmotic stress (Figure 5E, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5E, F.

claim: The polyUb accumulation phenotype in KO cells was partially rescued by overexpression of WT UCH37.
source: This phenotype was partially rescued by overexpression of WT UCH37.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data showing reduced polyUb accumulation in WT-expressing cells compared to KO.

claim: The loss of UCH37 negatively impacts proteasome degradation capacity in cells.
source: These results suggest that the loss of UCH37 negatively impacts proteasome degradation capacity in cells.
evidence: This is inferred from observations of increased polyUb accumulation and proteasome foci in UCH37 KO cells.

claim: C88A and EWI cells accumulate K48, K11/K48 and, to a lesser extent, total polyUb conjugates both with and without osmotic stress.
source: From the whole-cell lysates, it was apparent that C88A and EWI cells accumulate K48, K11/K48 and, to a lesser extent, total polyUb conjugates; this was the case both with and without osmotic stress (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The C88A proteasomes accumulated polyUb conjugates, while the EWI proteasomes behaved similar to WT.
source: Whereas the C88A proteasomes accumulated polyUb conjugates, surprisingly, the EWI proteasomes behaved similar to WT.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data showing differential polyUb accumulation on C88A versus EWI proteasomes.

claim: Both free and conjugated Ub species accumulated on C88A proteasomes at levels 4 times that of WT or EWI proteasomes.
source: We found that both free and conjugated Ub species accumulated on C88A proteasomes at levels 4 times that of WT or EWI proteasomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative tUI-based assay data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The increased polyUb on C88A proteasomes was accompanied by increased association of the substrate shuttle receptor, RAD23B.
source: Additionally, the increased polyUb on C88A proteasomes was accompanied by increased association of the substrate shuttle receptor, RAD23B (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Although neither the C88A nor EWI form of UCH37 can catalyze deubiquitination, only the C88A proteasomes fail to clear Ub species efficiently.
source: These results suggest that, although neither the C88A nor EWI form of UCH37 can catalyze deubiquitination, only the C88A proteasomes fail to clear Ub species efficiently.
evidence: This is inferred from observations that C88A but not EWI proteasomes accumulate polyUb.

claim: C88A proteasomes in the condensates are significantly more static than WT or EWI proteasomes.
source: Given that the reported t1/2 of proteasomes in sucrose-induced foci is 13.71 s (Yasuda et al., 2020), similar to that of UCH37 WT, these data suggest that C88A proteasomes in the condensates are significantly more static.
evidence: This is inferred from FRAP data showing slower recovery times for C88A compared to WT and EWI.

claim: Among dynamically associated proteasome-interacting proteins (PIPs), Ub (UBA52), RAD23B, PA28 (PSME1 and PSME2), USP14, and 19S assembly chaperones (PSMD5 and PSMD10) were noticeably enriched in the C88S and, to a lesser extent, EWI proteasomes.
source: However, among dynamically associated proteasome-interacting proteins (PIPs), we found that Ub (UBA52), RAD23B, PA28 (PSME1 and PSME2), USP14, and 19S assembly chaperones (PSMD5 and PSMD10) were noticeably enriched in the C88S and, to a lesser extent, EWI proteasomes (Figure 6F).
evidence: This claim is supported by TMT mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: RAD23B does not differentiate linear versus branched Ub3 provided that a K48 linkage is present within the chain.
source: We found that RAD23B does not differentiate linear versus branched Ub3 provided that a K48 linkage is present within the chain (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscale thermophoresis binding data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: RPN13's interaction with the ASCL promotes a conformation that prevents linear polyUb chains from accessing the active site.
source: In the ground state, RPN13's interaction with the ASCL promotes a conformation that prevents linear polyUb chains from accessing the active site.
evidence: This is inferred from mutagenesis data showing that ASCL mutations affect RPN13's ability to suppress linear chain hydrolysis.

claim: The ASCL functions as a gate and RPN13 as a gatekeeper to prevent unintended hydrolysis of linear polyUb chains.
source: Thus, the ASCL functions as a gate and RPN13 as a gatekeeper to prevent unintended hydrolysis of linear polyUb chains.
evidence: This is a model inferred from experimental data showing RPN13's role in restricting linear chain access.

claim: Upon encountering branched chains, UCH37 engages the hydrophobic patches of both distal Ub units; this would enhance affinity and affect the displacement of the ASCL to allow access to the active site.
source: Upon encountering branched chains, UCH37 engages the hydrophobic patches of both distal Ub units; this would enhance affinity and, crucially, affect the displacement of the ASCL to allow access to the active site.
evidence: This is a model based on NMR and biochemical data showing engagement of both distal Ub hydrophobic patches.

claim: The geometry of a branched polyUb chain likely plays a key role in substrate binding, position of the ASCL, and K48 specificity in debranching by UCH37–RPN13.
source: The geometry of a branched polyUb chain likely plays a key role in substrate binding, position of the ASCL, and K48 specificity in debranching by UCH37–RPN13.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed substrate preferences and structural considerations.

claim: The K6/K48-branched Ub3 presents a favorable configuration to engage and activate the enzyme.
source: Our data suggest that the K6/K48-branched Ub3 presents a favorable configuration to engage and activate the enzyme.
evidence: This is inferred from data showing preferential binding and catalysis with K6/K48-branched chains.

claim: The configuration of the two distal Ubs at the branch point directs specificity for cleavage of the K48 linkage.
source: Given that we did not observe significant NMR CSPs of Ub residues around the K48 linkage on the proximal Ub, we favor a model in which the configuration of the two distal Ubs at the branch point directs specificity for cleavage of the K48 linkage.
evidence: This is a model inferred from NMR data showing limited perturbations around the K48 linkage on the proximal Ub.

claim: PolyUb substrates with Ub units branching from different lysine residues will not be hydrolyzed with equal efficiencies.
source: Our model predicts that only some of these possible structures are ideal substrates for UCH37–RPN13; thus, polyUb substrates with Ub units branching from different lysine residues will not be hydrolyzed with equal efficiencies.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the observed differential efficiencies with different branched substrates.

claim: The efficiency of substrate disassembly is in the order of K6/K48 > K11/K48 >> K63/K48.
source: The finding that the efficiency of substrate disassembly is in the order of K6/K48 > K11/K48 >> K63/K48 supports this idea.
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic data showing different catalytic efficiencies for different branched substrates.

claim: UCH37 has at least two Ub-binding sites, each engaging the hydrophobic patch of a distal Ub unit in a branched chain.
source: Using K6/K48 Ub3 as a model, our NMR experiments suggest that UCH37 has at least two Ub-binding sites, each engaging the hydrophobic patch of a distal Ub unit in a branched chain.
evidence: This is inferred from NMR data showing perturbations in both distal Ubs.

claim: One of the Ub-binding sites, presumably the S1 site, is occupied in the complex with monoUb described in previous crystal structures.
source: One of these sites, presumably the S1 site, is occupied in the complex with monoUb described in previous crystal structures (Vander Linden et al., 2015; Sahtoe et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on prior crystal structures showing monoUb binding.

claim: Additional perturbations of surface residues in the Ub α-helix, most notably K29, D32, and E34, may represent new interactions with the S1 site that are promoted upon binding the branched chain.
source: Unexpectedly, we observed additional perturbations of surface residues in the Ub α-helix, most notably K29, D32, and E34, which may represent new interactions with the S1 site that are promoted upon binding the branched chain.
evidence: This is speculative interpretation of NMR data showing perturbations not seen in crystal structures with monoUb.

claim: Debranching did not depend on the hydrophobic patch of the proximal Ub.
source: In contrast, debranching did not depend on the hydrophobic patch of the proximal Ub.
evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis data showing that L8A,I44A mutations in the proximal Ub do not affect debranching.

claim: The proximal Ub serves primarily to position the distal Ub units rather than interact directly with the enzyme.
source: We also observed significantly smaller perturbations of NMR signals in the proximal Ub upon binding of K6/K48 Ub3 to UCH37–RPN13C, suggesting that the proximal Ub serves primarily to position the distal Ub units rather than interact directly with the enzyme.
evidence: This is inferred from NMR data showing smaller perturbations in the proximal Ub compared to distal Ubs.

claim: It is possible that the proximal Ub is responsible for displacing the ASCL in concert with positioning of the distal Ub units.
source: It is also possible that the proximal Ub is responsible for displacing the ASCL in concert with positioning of the distal Ub units.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the potential role of the proximal Ub.

claim: The affinities between the several branched Ub3 chains tested and UCH37–RPN13C are generally weak.
source: The affinities between the several branched Ub3 chains we tested and UCH37–RPN13C are generally weak; these were either measured directly as KDs or inferred from KM values.
evidence: This is based on binding and kinetic data showing KD and KM values in the micromolar range.

claim: Efficient debranching in vivo likely requires additional interactions that bring or retain polyUb–protein substrates onto the 26S proteasome.
source: Thus, efficient debranching in vivo likely requires additional interactions that bring or retain polyUb–protein substrates onto the 26S proteasome.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observation of weak in vitro binding affinities.

claim: It is possible that longer polyUb chains engage the PRU domain of full-length RPN13.
source: Although we did not observe differences in activities between UCH37–RPN13C and UCH37–RPN13FL with a Ub3 substrate, it is possible that longer polyUb chains engage the PRU domain.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about potential interactions with longer chains.

claim: At least a subset of proteins in stress-induced inclusions are modified with branched polyUb chains.
source: Upon osmotic or oxidative stresses, we observed cellular inclusions that contain proteasomes and are stained by a K11/K48-bispecific antibody, suggesting that at least a subset of proteins in those inclusions are modified with branched polyUb chains.
evidence: This is inferred from immunofluorescence data showing K11/K48 staining in proteasome-containing inclusions.

claim: Debranching by UCH37 promotes the dissolution of proteasome degradation centers.
source: We conclude that debranching by UCH37 promotes the dissolution of proteasome degradation centers.
evidence: This is inferred from observations that loss of UCH37 activity increases proteasome foci while WT UCH37 decreases them.

claim: In the absence of debranching activity, UCH37 interactions with the polyUb species lead to their retention at the proteasome, which in turn abnormally retains other dynamic PIPs such as RAD23B and USP14.
source: These observations suggest that, in the absence of debranching activity, UCH37 interactions with the polyUb species lead to their retention at the proteasome, which in turn abnormally retains other dynamic PIPs such as RAD23B and USP14.
evidence: This is inferred from observations that C88A proteasomes accumulate polyUb, RAD23B, and USP14, and show slower dynamics.

claim: UCH37 functions to clear polyUb chains, most likely those that contain branches, from the proteasome.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that UCH37 functions to clear polyUb chains, most likely those that contain branches, from the proteasome (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a model inferred from multiple lines of evidence showing UCH37's debranching activity and effects on proteasome function.

claim: Branched polyUb can promote substrate degradation by enhancing targeting to either p97/VCP or proteasomes.
source: It has been shown that branched polyUb can promote substrate degradation by enhancing targeting to either p97/VCP or proteasomes (Yau et al., 2017; Meyer and Rape, 2014), although the underlying mechanism is unclear.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Proteasome-associated UCH37 could efficiently disassemble branched Ub chains by severing the K48 linkage at branch points, thereby shortening the chains and also promoting chain release because most proteasomal Ub receptors prefer chains with K48 linkages.
source: Proteasome-associated UCH37 could efficiently disassemble these Ub chains by severing the K48 linkage at branch points, thereby shortening the chains and also promoting chain release because most proteasomal Ub receptors prefer chains with K48 linkages (Shi et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2020; Tsuchiya et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a model based on UCH37's debranching activity and known properties of proteasomal Ub receptors.

claim: This model of UCH37 function requires that debranching is slow enough to not compete with substrate targeting, engagement, and the initiation of degradation.
source: This model of UCH37 function requires that debranching is slow enough to not compete with substrate targeting, engagement, and the initiation of degradation.
evidence: This is a logical requirement of the proposed model.

claim: With a kcat of 3.2 min−1 or less, deubiquitination by UCH37 is unlikely to cause premature release of polyUb–protein substrates from the 26S proteasome.
source: For the in vitro degradation of a small model substrate such as titin-I27, substrate processing is complete in less than 1 min (Bard et al., 2019). Thus, with a kcat of 3.2 min−1 or less, deubiquitination by UCH37 is unlikely to cause premature release of polyUb–protein substrates from the 26S proteasome.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of UCH37 kinetics with substrate processing rates.

claim: USP14 exhibits much faster kinetics than UCH37 and can remove the Ub signal prior to substrate commitment.
source: This is in contrast to USP14, another proteasome-associated DUB, which exhibits much faster kinetics and can remove the Ub signal prior to substrate commitment.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about USP14 function.

claim: Binding to multiple Ub receptor sites on the proteasome may slow or stall substrate translocation; debranching by UCH37 could help to alleviate that problem.
source: In another scenario, it is also possible that binding to multiple Ub receptor sites on the proteasome slows or stalls substrate translocation; debranching by UCH37 could help to alleviate that problem.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about an alternative mechanism for UCH37 function.
